Telangana rain deficit shrinks to 10%, IMD issues red alert in 5 districts
After weeks of below-normal rainfall, Telangana has witnessed a strong revival of the monsoon, significantly improving its overall rainfall figures. While the showers have benefited agriculture, they have also caused widespread disruptions, prompting a red alert in five districts and a work-from-home advisory in parts of Hyderabad.

Telangana has received widespread rainfall over the past few days after a prolonged spell of deficient rain, bringing relief to farmers and improving the state's overall rainfall position. The rainfall deficiency, which stood at 33 per cent till 15 days ago, narrowed to 10 per cent by Thursday morning, according to the India Meteorological Department.
At the same time, the fresh spell of rain has affected normal life in parts of the state, including Hyderabad, where waterlogging and traffic snarls were reported on the night of July 29. With more rain forecast, the IMD issued a 'red alert' for isolated places in five districts, while the Cyberabad Traffic Police advised companies and organisations to consider work from home wherever possible.
According to the Telangana Development Planning Society, Gullakota in Jagtial district received 70.5 mm of rainfall till noon on Thursday, followed by 66.6 mm at Sirpur (U) in Kumram Bheem Asifabad district. Even so, 13 of the state's 33 districts have received less than 20 per cent of their normal rainfall so far. The deficiency in Yadadri-Bhuvanagiri district is as high as 65 per cent, while rainfall remains deficient in Hyderabad as of date.
Rain also pushed rivulets into spate at some places in the state, disrupting normal life. In its weather warning, the IMD issued a 'red alert' for isolated places in Adilabad, Kumram Bheem Asifabad, Mancherial, Nirmal and Jagtial districts, forecasting very heavy to extremely heavy rainfall accompanied by strong surface winds from 1 pm on Thursday to 8.30 am on July 31. It said light to moderate rain or thundershowers are likely at most places over Telangana during the same period.
The IMD said a 'red alert' indicates extremely heavy rainfall of over 204 mm in 24 hours. In view of the forecast for moderate to heavy rainfall, the Cyberabad Traffic Police, in an advisory, asked companies and organisations operating in the area to consider work from home wherever possible. It also asked them to follow staggered early logouts from 2 pm onwards to minimise travel-related risks, ease pressure on road infrastructure and ensure smooth functioning of essential services amid the adverse weather.
In a post on X, the Cyberabad Traffic Police said the advisory was issued keeping in mind safety, productivity, the likelihood of severe traffic congestion, and the need for uninterrupted emergency services. Overall, the fresh rains have improved Telangana's rainfall position and brought cheer to farmers, even as several districts remain deficient and authorities stay alert over the impact of heavy rain.

Centre outlines relief measures to cushion airlines from rising ATF prices in Lok Sabha reply
Civil Aviation Minister Kinjarapu Rammohan Naidu said the government, after consultations with stakeholders, introduced multiple interventions aimed at supporting the aviation sector and keeping air travel affordable.
The Centre on Thursday informed the Lok Sabha that it has rolled out a series of measures to cushion domestic airlines from the impact of rising Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF) prices, including temporary price caps, airport charge relief, liquidity support and tax reductions, while also approving a one-time Rs. 10,000 crore ATF Price Stabilisation Fund as a contingency measure.
Replying to a starred question raised by MPs Janardan Mishra and Satish Kumar Gautam, Civil Aviation Minister Kinjarapu Rammohan Naidu said the government, after consultations with stakeholders, introduced multiple interventions aimed at supporting the aviation sector and keeping air travel affordable.
According to the statement laid on the Table of the House, ATF prices for domestic operations were capped at a maximum increase of 25% over the March 1, 2026 base price. The cap came into effect from April 1, 2026, and remained applicable during April and May 2026.
The minister also said the government provided partial deferment of airport landing and parking charges for domestic operations at major airports. In addition, airlines received a 25% rebate on these charges at Airports Authority of India (AAI) airports.
As part of financial assistance, the government approved Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS) 5.0 with a total corpus of Rs. 18,100 crore, including Rs. 5,000 crore earmarked for Indian airlines to provide liquidity support.
The Centre further highlighted that Value Added Tax (VAT) on ATF was reduced for six months in two key States -- from 25% to 7% in Delhi and from 18% to 7% in Maharashtra.
The Lok Sabha reply further stated that the government approved a one-time ATF Price Stabilisation Fund (PSF) Scheme with budgetary support of up to Rs. 10,000 crore.
The fund was conceived as a contingency response to the exceptional increase in international ATF prices triggered by the West Asia crisis, with the objective of protecting domestic airlines and ensuring operational stability.
However, according to an NDTV Profit report citing sources, the scheme has failed to attract any participating airline since its approval on June 3, 2026. "No airline has signed a memorandum of understanding under the scheme," sources told the publication.
The report said the scheme proposed capping the benchmark domestic ATF price in Delhi at Rs. 115 per litre for participating airlines for up to three years.
With market-linked crude oil prices easing after the spike witnessed during the West Asia conflict, officials said the immediate need for such intervention has diminished.
"The scheme may now be kept in abeyance. However, it can be revived if global oil prices remain elevated or fresh geopolitical disruptions lead to sustained fuel price spikes," another person familiar with the discussions was quoted as saying by NDTV Profit.

IMD heavy rain alert Ahmedabad: Schools, colleges to remain closed as weather dept issues red alert for July 31
All schools and colleges in Ahmedabad will remain closed on July 31 as a precautionary measure following the IMD’s Red Alert for extremely heavy rainfall across Gujarat.
All schools and colleges in Ahmedabad will remain shut on Friday as the administration declared a holiday amid a Red Alert forecast for extremely heavy rainfall and possible weather-related risks. The closure applies to all government schools, grant-in-aid and private educational institutions, including primary, secondary and higher secondary schools, as well as colleges across Ahmedabad city.
The weather department has forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall across eight Gujarat districts on Friday, July 31. The affected areas include Ahmedabad, Surat, Vadodara, Anand, Bharuch, Narmada, Tapi, and Dang. The directive was issued by the District Education Officer (DEO), Ahmedabad, based on instructions from the Ahmedabad Collector, who cited the IMD’s forecast of heavy to very heavy rainfall and prioritised the safety of students.
Schools and colleges have been asked to promptly communicate the holiday announcement to students, parents, and staff using WhatsApp, SMS, phone calls, or other platforms. Officials said decisions regarding further operations will be taken based on the evolving weather situation and instructions issued by the authorities.
Authorities said the closure was announced as a preventive measure to protect students and school staff in view of the expected intense rainfall over the next few days. Officials clarified that further decisions on school and college operations will be taken after reviewing weather conditions and will be communicated separately. Institutions have been advised to rely only on official instructions released by the district authorities.
IMD forecasts extreme heavy rainfall across Gujarat
The IMD has sounded a Red Alert for Ahmedabad and multiple districts across Gujarat, predicting heavy to extremely heavy rainfall for the next four days. The forecast suggests Ahmedabad could receive nearly eight inches of rain on Friday, while Narmada may witness rainfall of up to 12 inches. Authorities have issued a special warning for areas at risk of extreme weather conditions.
The IMD has attributed the expected weather conditions to the combined influence of multiple meteorological systems, including a deep depression, an active monsoon trough, a shear zone, a western disturbance and an offshore trough. These systems are likely to trigger widespread and intense rainfall across the state. Fishermen have also been advised not to venture into the sea for the next two days due to rough weather conditions.
